evals.prompt: Create a NodeJS Express backend with Veracity login. I want the default OpenID Connect (BFF) strategy.
evals.expected_output: Baseline scaffolded via web-backend-node (no project existed), then OIDC BFF auth layered on: @azure/msal-node confidential client, express-session with __Host- cookie, auth routes, env vars added, secrets guided into .env.local.
assertions: Strategy determined as OpenID Connect (from user request)
No existing project detected -> baseline scaffolded first (web-backend-node conventions: helmet, health endpoints, /api/v1 anchor, zod env config)
package.json includes express, @azure/msal-node, express-session, helmet, zod
src/auth/msalClient.ts created (ConfidentialClientApplication)
src/auth/authRoutes.ts created with /auth, /auth/challenge, /auth/callback, /api/me, /signOut
Session cookie name uses __Host- prefix (e.g. __Host-veracity.session) with secure + path=/
Unauthenticated /api/* returns 401 instead of redirecting (authMiddleware)
env files contain B2C Production values (B2C_INSTANCE, B2C_DOMAIN, B2C_TENANT_ID, CLIENT_ID)
SESSION_SECRET auto-generated (strong 32-byte random) and written as a real value in .env.local; CLIENT_SECRET written as a placeholder for the user to fill (not asked to paste in chat)
.gitignore ignores .env.local

evals.prompt: Set up a stateless NodeJS API that validates Veracity JWT bearer tokens.
evals.expected_output: Express + TypeScript project with jose-based JWT Bearer validation middleware, no session, env with JWT_AUTHORITY and JWT_AUDIENCE.
assertions: Strategy determined as JWT Bearer (from 'stateless' and 'bearer tokens' phrasing)
package.json includes jose
src/auth/jwtMiddleware.ts created (createRemoteJWKSet + jwtVerify)
clockTolerance set to 60 seconds (matches .NET 1-minute ClockSkew)
No express-session, no authRoutes (JWT is stateless)
env contains JWT_AUTHORITY and JWT_AUDIENCE
User asked for the API Client ID (Audience)
No CLIENT_SECRET collected (JWT only validates tokens)

evals.prompt: I want Veracity auth in my Node app but I don't have an app registration yet.
evals.expected_output: Skill scaffolds auth files and directs the user to Veracity developer docs to register their application.
assertions: Output includes links to docs.veracity.com developer documentation
Output includes getting-started-as-a-developer link
Output includes create-an-application link
Auth files still scaffolded (skill does not block on missing registration)
CLIENT_ID left as a placeholder for the user to fill in
User told which values they will need (Client ID, Client Secret)

evals.prompt: Add Veracity OIDC login to my Node app and also let it call the Veracity API V3 for services and notifications.
evals.expected_output: OIDC BFF auth plus Veracity API V3 typed client (openapi-typescript + openapi-fetch) and BFF proxy endpoints.
assertions: OIDC strategy selected
openapi-typescript and openapi-fetch added; veracity:gen script present
src/veracity/veracityApiMiddleware.ts created with Bearer + Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key injection
src/veracity/apiV3Routes.ts created with /api/services and /api/notifications/count
Downstream token obtained via MSAL acquireTokenSilent using VERACITY_API_SCOPE
env contains VERACITY_API_V3_BASE_URL and VERACITY_API_SCOPE (Production values)
User guided to set VERACITY_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY in .env.local (not asked to paste in chat)

evals.prompt: Create a Veracity OIDC Node backend that runs across multiple instances behind a load balancer.
evals.expected_output: OIDC BFF auth with a Redis-backed session store for multi-instance session sharing.
assertions: OIDC strategy selected
connect-redis and ioredis added (multi-instance explicitly required)
express-session configured with a RedisStore
User guided to set REDIS_URL via .env.local (treated as a secret)
Explanation that Redis session store is the equivalent of .NET Redis Data Protection

Existing project structure preserved (app.ts/server.ts not wholesale replaced)

Dependencies added to existing package.json without clobbering existing deps
env values merged without overwriting existing configuration
helmet and session middleware inserted at the correct position in the pipeline
User asked for the Client ID

evals.prompt: Add auth to my Node service. It's a bearer-token API consumed by other services, not a website.
evals.expected_output: Skill identifies JWT Bearer from the phrasing and configures stateless validation without OIDC session/login.
assertions: Skill identifies JWT Bearer strategy from phrasing

jose used for JWKS validation against JWT_AUTHORITY
Token lifetime, issuer, and audience validated

msalClient.ts and authRoutes.ts created

evals.prompt: I have an existing Fastify + TypeScript API. Add Veracity OpenID Connect login (BFF) to it.
evals.expected_output: OIDC BFF auth integrated idiomatically into the existing Fastify app using the Fastify adapter (plugins + preHandler hook), no baseline re-scaffold, no express-session.
assertions: Existing project detected as Fastify -> web-backend-node NOT invoked to re-scaffold
Fastify adapter set copied (assets/core/* + assets/fastify/*), NOT the Express assets
@fastify/session and @fastify/cookie added (NOT express-session)
Session registered with __Host-veracity.session cookie (secure, httpOnly, sameSite, path=/)
authRoutes registered as a Fastify plugin; requireAuth applied as a preHandler
trustProxy enabled on the Fastify instance
Unauthenticated /api/* returns 401 (preHandler), health routes stay anonymous
SESSION_SECRET auto-generated and written as a real value in .env.local; CLIENT_SECRET written as a placeholder for the user; session secret is required (no hard-coded fallback in code)

SESSION_SECRET auto-generated and written as a real value in .env.local; CLIENT_SECRET written as a placeholder for the user; session secret is required (no hard-coded fallback in code)
